title: Telemetry Terraform module: Prometheus+Grafana, OTEL collector, and log-forwarder with healthchecks and safe upgrade path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module to provision the full telemetry stack inside customer VPCs: Prometheus server (and node exporters), Grafana instance (with provisioning), OpenTelemetry Collector (otel-collector) for traces/metrics, and a log-forwarder (vector/fluentbit) that ships to our central log ingestion endpoint. The module must: (1) be usable for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments, (2) support safe, automated upgrades with minimal downtime, (3) expose standardized healthchecks and readiness probes, (4) include opinionated defaults for resource sizing and retention but allow overrides, and (5) provide CI checks + integration tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terraform module lives under modules/telemetry with submodules: prometheus, grafana, otel_collector, log_forwarder. 2) Module can be invoked with minimal variables to create a working stack in a VPC subnet. 3) Each component exposes a /health or /-/ready endpoint that is validated by a module-managed kubernetes or consul healthcheck resource. 4) Upgrade strategy: default uses rolling update with configurable max_unavailable and a canary boolean + canary_count; when canary=true terraform apply will create canary replica(s) and route a percentage of traffic via service mesh weights (or DNS split) for 10 minutes before switching. 5) Automated plan checks in CI must fail on destructive changes to stateful data (Prometheus PVC resize, retention changes) unless --allow-destructive is explicitly provided and reviewed. 6) Module includes example consumption snippet and integration tests that run in CI against a ephemeral Kind/EKS test cluster. 7) Documentation: README with variables, outputs, upgrade notes, and a short runbook for operational troubleshooting.
design_decisions:
- Implementation: Terraform module exposing both helm_release (Helm provider) and kubernetes_manifest paths to support clusters without Tiller. Default is Helm for managed clusters; manifest path for air-gapped customers.
- Prometheus: use kube-prometheus-stack helm chart but pin chart version and provide a chart_overrides map. Persistence enabled with configurable storage_class + size. Retention default 15d.
- Grafana: provision data sources and dashboards via provisioning config mapped from module inputs. Admin password generated by module unless provided. Admin endpoints locked to internal subnets by default.
- OTEL Collector: use a composable configuration with receivers (prometheus, OTLP), processors (batch, memory_limiter), and exporters (redwood-ingest). Collector runs as a Deployment with readiness/liveness endpoints (/metrics and /healthz).
- Log forwarder: vector as default (FluentBit opt-in). Vector runs as a DaemonSet when shipping node logs and as a Deployment when shipping application logs.
- Healthchecks: implement Kubernetes Pod readiness/liveness + an external k8s Service HealthCheck resource that can be wired into our VPC load balancer health-checks; also emit a /metadata endpoint with version and build info for rollback safety.
- Upgrades: don't rely on Terraform to do destructive upgrades. Introduce explicit variable 'allow_data_migration' and 'upgrade_strategy' enum [rolling, blue_green, canary]. For blue_green we create new resources with suffix and switch service selector; for canary we add weighted routing via service mesh (if available) or advisory NGINX config snippets.
- Backwards compatibility: module will maintain input names but accept legacy 'prometheus_enabled' -> now 'prometheus.enabled' map via transition layer.
implementation_notes: - File layout: modules/telemetry/{prometheus,grafana,otel_collector,log_forwarder}/main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf + examples/complete/usage.tf. - CI: terraform validate + tflint + terraform-plan-checker (fail on changes to retention or PVC unless SKIP_SAFE_CHECKS=true). - Integration tests: separate pipeline job that deploys into a disposable EKS cluster (eksctl), runs smoke checks: scrape target present, grafana login, otel metrics ingestion end-to-end, log tailing verification. - Secret handling: sensitive values must be passed via SSM/Secrets Manager references; module supports kms_key_id for encryption of generated secrets. - Docs: Confluence design at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/TelemetryTerraformModule (internal), example GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428 (draft).
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: Prometheus retention and PVC changes can cause data loss on careless upgrades. Mitigation: block terraform apply for retention/pvc size reductions unless explicit flag set and run preflight snapshot job. - Risk: Grafana admin password rotation could lock customers out. Mitigation: default to generated secret stored in customer's KMS-backed secret store and rotate via separate job. - Risk: OTEL collector misconfiguration can drop traces. Mitigation: include default processor chain with memory_limiter and observability metrics for the collector itself; add alerting rule that fires on dropped_batches > threshold. - Risk: Air-gapped customers need chart tarballs. Mitigation: support chart_package variable and local_chart_path override.
